title: Official-tier ingest health: non-zero exits + an ingest-runs freshness sentinel
detail: Make run() exit non-zero when any official source records status='error' (Cloud Run max_retries=2 and execution-failure alerting then work for free), and add a monthly CI freshness check over house_price_ingest_runs (age of last ok per source vs expected cadence) mirroring the economy platform's sentinel ($economy-data skill, 'monthly CI red = real alarm'). This one change would have caught the live vg_nsw/vg_vic breakage on day one.

title: Wire price_index_derived into /housing and retire the frozen RPPI tile
detail: The current-quarter national + per-state derived index (531 rows, live to 2026-03-31, refreshed monthly) already exists in prod precisely for this — swap the '8-capital price index (to 2021)' BigStat and add a HousingSeriesChart for it (format='index' already supported). Zero new ingest work; pure read-path wiring in web/src/app/housing/page.tsx.

title: Rates & credit panel from already-ingested RBA series
detail: cash_rate (432 rows, monthly to 2026-07-31), mortgage_rate_oo/investor (F6), housing_credit_growth ×3 (D1) and the E1 household balance sheet are all in house_prices with no reader. A '/housing' rates panel (cash rate vs outstanding mortgage rates vs credit growth) is a pure frontend + one-RPC job — note mv_housing_headline is quarterly-only (period_freq='Q' filter, 000053:67), so monthly series need GetHousePriceSeries or an MV tweak.

title: Harden refresh_housing_materialized_views to the 000095 pattern
detail: One migration: function-scoped SET statement_timeout TO '0', per-MV guards including mv_housing_headline, and WHEN query_canceled OR OTHERS everywhere. The shorts refresh already proved this pattern after a 19-day silent-staleness incident; the housing function is the last refresh routine without it.

title: Content-hash-driven change detection and revalidation gating
detail: Add 'WHERE house_prices.content_hash IS DISTINCT FROM EXCLUDED.content_hash' to upsertObservations and return (upserted, changed) counts. This gives per-run 'new ABS quarter landed: N changed rows' logging, makes fetched_at meaningful (currently rewritten on every row every run), lets pingRevalidate fire only on real change (making the TF module's comment true), and provides the signal for a 'new quarter' hook (e.g. auto-tweet / newsroom prompt when a new RES_DWELL quarter arrives).

title: Append-only ingest run history
detail: Replace the PK-per-source overwrite in house_price_ingest_runs with (or add alongside) an append-only history table (source, started_at, status, rows, last_period, detail). Enables 'last success age' queries, failure-streak detection, and post-incident forensics — today it is impossible to tell when vg_vic last succeeded from the cursor table alone. Cheap: the collector already funnels every outcome through updateRun().

title: Wire lease reclaim + collector heartbeat renew into the queue coupling
detail: Both halves already exist unused: brandbrain has ReclaimExpired (re-pend expired in_progress with attempts left, fail the exhausted) and a Renew endpoint; the collector has a natural heartbeat point (per-page loop in sweepSuburbSource). Calling ReclaimExpired lazily at the top of Claim plus a per-suburb Renew from crawl_agent.go permanently closes outage mode #4 (orphaned leases) including the dry-run-claim orphan case, with no schema change (lease_expires_at is already populated).

title: Queue-vs-corpus reconciliation check: assert 'succeeded' implies data written
detail: The three silent stoppers (thin-suburb wedge, orphaned leases, circuit-open banked success) share one shape: the queue's terminal status diverges from what actually landed in property_listings. A read-only nightly job that joins brandbrain's succeeded jobs (by suburb/source/completed_at) against property_listings.last_seen_at and writes a mismatch count into crawl_run_status would have caught all three within a day. agentJobTerminal already encodes this instinct per-job; this generalises it across the system.

title: PageMeta-aware thin-page gate (replaces the MIN_PER_PAGE hand-tuning)
detail: REA's extractPageMeta already returns the portal's own exact on-target inventory count (OnTargetResults, present on 483/483 measured REA page-1 records). Using it to classify a sub-threshold page 1 — meta says <5 on-target → sweepComplete (genuine small suburb, delist-safe); meta absent or claims more → keep sweepBlocked — eliminates the thin-suburb false-block class the same way #404 used wantPages<softCap to fix REA delisting, and removes the CRAWL_LISTINGS_MIN_PER_PAGE=1 operational workaround.

title: Agent-app self-heal preflight in the scheduled wrappers
detail: The wrappers already do Chrome self-healing; the analogous auth self-heal is missing. Before draining: read ~/.brandbrain/diag-port, probe /control/v1/auth/session/export, and on failure `open -a /Applications/BrandBrainAgent.app`, wait ~20s, re-probe (the 30-day refresh token survives, so no re-login is needed). Closes outage mode #1 for scheduled runs — the exact failure that killed the crawl for 2+ days on 2026-08-01.

title: Trace-replay regression bench for sweep classification
detail: The #404 completeness fix was derived by hand from 861 light-mode traces / 3,179 page records. The pieces for automating that exist: trace.jsonl records every pagination signal + decision, and fileFetcher/CRAWL_LISTINGS_FIXTURE_DIR already replays saved HTML offline. A bench that replays a committed (sanitised, jsonl-only — no portal HTML) trace corpus through sweepSuburbSource and diffs the decision distribution would let future gate changes (like enhancement 3) be measured against real portal behaviour before deploy instead of after a fortnight of prod sweeps.

title: Unified crawl alerting: webhook the run-status transitions, not just freshness
detail: postFreshnessAlarm already implements a redaction-safe Slack/Discord POST helper. Reusing it from writeCrawlRunStatus when a round derives 'error', 'blocked', or 'rewarm' (deriveCrawlRunStatus) turns the existing health taxonomy into push alerts — an auth-dead rig or fully-blocked session then pages within one round instead of surfacing via a 72h freshness horizon on a dashboard nobody was watching during the August outages. Pair with setting CRAWL_FRESHNESS_WEBHOOK on the rigs.

title: Prod schema-drift sentinel for the hand-apply regime
detail: A read-only CI job (or make target) that connects to prod, introspects information_schema + pg_matviews for the tables/columns/MVs the committed store queries reference (house_prices, property_listings, suburb_demographics banner_*/crime columns, the 6 housing MV shapes), and fails red on mismatch. Directly de-fangs the class of incident already documented twice in-repo (000092's '000090 was hand-applied to prod' drift; the politicians allowlist landmine). The column list can be generated from the migrations dir so it stays current.

title: Housing MV refresh bookkeeping + admin-jobs surfacing
detail: Mirror the 000094 refreshed_at pattern: a small housing_mv_refresh_runs table (view_name, started_at, finished_at, concurrent bool, error text) written from inside refresh_housing_materialized_views(), merged into the existing /api/admin/jobs dashboard the way crawl_run_status (000089) already is. The 19-day silent-staleness incident on the shorts MVs shows exactly why per-view refresh outcomes need to be observable; today a failed housing refresh is only a collector log line on a residential Mac.

title: Time-anchored sold-price layer from status_change events
detail: property_price_events already records status_change transitions with observed_at, so a derived sold_at per listing is one query away. Build rolling 3/6/12-month sold aggregates (per suburb + state) to replace the unbounded 'sold' FILTERs in mv_suburb_listing_stats/mv_state_price_drops — and it unlocks a genuinely new surface: asking-vs-sold discount (final sold price vs first ask) per suburb, which no free AU site publishes and which the crawl corpus uniquely supports.

title: Ship the single-FY crime trend read path (Phase 3)
detail: suburb_crime_stats already stores the pooled=false per-FY series and the collector contains a ready reference reader (getSuburbCrime, store.go:478-508, whose comment says 'used by GetSuburbProfile once the Phase-3 read wiring lands'). Adding a gated crime-trend repeated field to GetSuburbProfile (same NOT small_pop/NOT unreliable/licence predicate as 000092) gives suburb profiles a multi-year crime sparkline from data that is already ingested and ranked — pure read wiring, no new pipeline.

title: Source-preference layer for mv_housing_headline (multi-tier medians)
detail: Rebuild the headline MV with a ranked DISTINCT ON per (region, measure, dwelling, period) before windowing (e.g. prefer abs_res_dwell > state VG > others). Beyond fixing the latent multi-source LAG trap, it is the schema prerequisite for the pending state-government tiers (house-price-multistate memory: NSW built, more states planned) to coexist with ABS on the same regions without corrupting QoQ/YoY — currently every new quarterly source must avoid every existing region×measure key.

title: Retention + BRIN policy for property_price_events
detail: Every sweep appends events forever; all read paths and MVs window at most 365 days (drill-down cap) and usually 30. Add a BRIN index on observed_at (near-free, the table is append-ordered) and a cleanup function pruning events older than ~18 months for delisted listings — same pattern as the news 90-day TTL (migration 000029). Keeps refresh and the firstp/address-board scans flat as the corpus compounds, before the table gets big enough that pruning itself becomes a Supabase pooler problem (cf. the 527k-row crime upsert chunking lesson).

title: Slug-resolution RPC for suburb pages
detail: Add ResolveSuburbSlug(state_code, slug) → sal_code (or a slug filter on ListStateSuburbs) and precompute the slug in suburb_demographics. Kills the pattern where every /housing/[state]/[suburb] SSR miss pulls the full ~5,000-row, 54-field state payload just to find one row (getHousing.ts:292-298). Pairs naturally with a redirect map for renamed suburbs.

title: Lightweight map-projection variant of ListStateSuburbs
detail: The state choropleth's 'Colour by' toggle needs ~6-8 fields per suburb per metric (highlight-metrics.ts), but ListStateSuburbs always ships all 31 summary + 23 amenity fields for up to 5,000 suburbs. A field-mask param or a ListStateSuburbMetrics(metric_key) RPC would cut the hot /housing/[state] payload substantially and make the per-suburb LATERAL price probe skippable for non-price metrics (postgres_house_prices.go:315-326).

title: Server action + KV layer for GetPropertyHistory
detail: The per-address history surface is client-only today (getHousingClient.ts:171-187); there is no server action in getHousing.ts. Adding one with the same skipForBuild + cache:housing: KV + never-cache-empty treatment as the drops boards would let /housing/property/[addressKey] render ISR with last-good protection, and the existing flush=housing event already busts the right prefix.

title: Shared request-normalization helper for housing handlers
detail: One helper (uppercase/trim state_code, whitelist sort, clamp limit/window_days) applied in every housing handler before both the cache key and the store call — the pattern ListAgencyPriceStats already proves (house_prices.go:680-693). Fixes the case-sensitivity inconsistency and the cache-key fanout class in one place, and gives the store clamps a single authoritative twin.

title: Wire window_days on ListSuburbPriceDrops via the existing event query
detail: The proto already reserves window_days (housing.proto:341) and ListSuburbDropListings already has the parametrized-window event SQL with the 0.40 sanity cap (postgres_house_prices.go:770-806). A windowed on-the-fly aggregate (fallback to the MV for the default 30d) would let the board answer 'cuts this week vs this quarter' — a real product axis the crawl data supports today.

title: REST (google.api.http) bindings for the 7 unexposed housing RPCs
detail: Only the 4 price-drops rpcs have google.api.http annotations (shorts.proto:693, 706, 719, 732 — 4 of the 9 total in the whole 86-rpc legacy service). Annotating GetHousingOverview/GetHousePriceSeries/ListStateSuburbs/GetSuburbProfile/ListHousingRegions/ListSuburbPriceDrops/ListSuburbDropListings gives paying API customers a consistent REST surface over the whole housing dataset and makes the OpenAPI docs complete.

title: Choropleth board on /price-drops (drop-share by state)
detail: Everything needed is already committed: ChoroplethMap supports continuous fills + legends, states.topojson (493KB, CF-edge-cached) is in /public/geo, and GetPriceDropsOverview already returns per-state drop share / median cut (StateDropsBoard consumes it as a table). A small ssr:false map shading states by dropSharePct with click-through to ?state= would give the flagship board the same visual identity as /housing and make the state comparison legible at a glance.

title: KV-backed slug→SAL resolution index (kills the 5,000-row lookup)
detail: resolveSuburbSalCode currently fetches the entire state's suburb list (up to 4,544 rows) just to find one slug — on the TTFB path of every suburb page AND the suburb OG card. A per-state {slug: sal} map cached in Upstash under cache:housing: (flushed by the existing ?flush=housing crawl ping) or a tiny ResolveSuburbSlug RPC turns this into a ~5ms GET, and is the prerequisite for cheaply re-enabling ISR on the 15k suburb pages (finding #2) and for static suburb OG cards.

title: generateStaticParams + post-deploy warm for the ~1,165 priced suburbs
detail: The priced suburbs are exactly the pages the sitemap promotes and the ones with the richest content (banners, blurbs, price-drop panels, crime layers). Pre-rendering them (the 115 crawl-catalog suburbs at minimum) with revalidate + the existing /api/static-pages/warm-cache + bailOnEmptyRender pattern (already proven on /housing, /price-drops, /economy) would give static TTFB on the highest-value housing URLs instead of today's two-RPC dynamic render.

title: Shared roving-tabindex keyboard layer for both housing maps
detail: One hook (arrow keys move the focused feature, Enter selects/drills, Escape resets; single tab stop) would fix both a11y findings at once and is reusable by the economy map explorer, which imports the same MapLegend/choropleth primitives. ChoroplethMap already has the per-feature focus→highlight plumbing (onFocus→setHover at choropleth-map.tsx:245) to build on.

title: Data-driven state OG cards (median + YoY on the silhouette)
detail: /housing/[state]/opengraph-image already renders the state boundary silhouette but with static copy. getHousingOverview is KV-cached (24h TTL) and carries each capital's median + YoY/QoQ — overlaying '$941k median · +4.2% yr' would match the per-suburb card's median treatment and make state shares meaningfully richer for ~20 lines of code.

title: Suburb comparison surface (/housing/compare)
detail: suburb-profile.tsx already computes baselines deltas (suburb vs state vs national) and a nearest-6 'similar suburbs' rail (backend similarSuburbs z-score space), and state-suburb-explorer already normalises 40+ metrics into SuburbDatum with the highlight-metrics registry. A 2-3 suburb side-by-side (URL-driven, like the existing stock /compare) would reuse all of it and is a natural internal-linking magnet for the 1,165 priced-suburb pages.

title: Docs-drift guard test for collector modes
detail: A small Go test in services/house-price-collector (same pattern as the proto dual-add contract enforced by proto_parity_test.go) that parses main.go's mode switch (or a shared []string modes registry) and asserts every mode name appears in docs/feature/housing/pipeline.md and deploy/README.md. This mechanically prevents the exact defect found here (monolith at 7/22, CLAUDE.md at 11/22 mode coverage) and fails the deploy-gating test run when someone adds a mode without documenting it.

title: Shrink CLAUDE.md's housing section to a politicians-style pointer block
detail: The politicians CLAUDE.md section proves the shape: ~30 lines of rules-that-shape-everything + landmines + a pointer to docs/feature/politicians/. The housing section is ~3x longer and carries five enumerated lists (modes, RPCs, migrations, key files, gotchas) that all drifted. Once docs/feature/housing/ exists, replacing the section cuts always-loaded token weight in every session and removes four of the drift surfaces found in this audit.

title: An 'OUT — settled, not deferred' rulings section in the new data-sources.md
detail: Politicians' data-sources.md has a decisive ruled-out section (LinkedIn/X/Hansard) that prevents re-proposal. Housing's equivalent rulings exist but are scattered across memory files: ASX T+1 gross short sales (REJECTED 2026-07-28, do-not-re-propose), property.com.au ToS ban on aggregators, residential proxies (rejected — block is fingerprint-scoped), REA/Domain no-republish (source_licence gate), CRAWL_TRACE artifacts local-only, wa-tou-noncommercial exclusion (000092). Consolidating them with the reasoning makes each ruling durable and citable.

title: Dated corpus stat line generated from -mode freshness
detail: crawl_freshness.go already computes per-suburb coverage read-only from prod. Extend its output with a one-line corpus summary (total property_listings, covered suburbs, price events, as-at date) that operators paste into the docs/feature/housing/README.md header — mirroring politicians' 'Prod, as at 2026-07-31: 17,153 rows...' line. Eliminates the three contradictory undated counts (~22k / ~12,151 / ~12k) found in prose.

title: Package README for services/house-price-collector
detail: Two screens at the package root: what the binary is, the 22 modes grouped into their 7 families (official / census / electoral / listings-crawl / property-AVM / crime / local-insights), which env vars gate each family, and pointers to deploy/README.md (rig ops) and docs/feature/housing/ (architecture). Grounded in the fact the package has ~110 Go files and currently zero orientation docs.

title: Machine-readable mode registry powering both main.go usage and pipeline.md
detail: main.go's flag usage string and 22-way switch are hand-maintained in parallel. A single []modeSpec{name, family, writes, envs, timeout} table in main.go can drive the flag usage, the switch dispatch, the default-timeout selection (the agent/listings/crime 240-min cases already special-case by name), and a `-mode help` JSON dump that a script renders into the pipeline.md mode table — making the docs a build artifact of the code rather than a copy.

title: Centralise the licence gate in a house_prices_public SQL view
detail: The source_licence <> 'proprietary-tos-restricted' predicate is hand-copied 10 times across postgres_house_prices.go, and history shows it gets forgotten (the 2026-07 audit found 3+ missing sites). Migration 000092 already proved the pattern for crime: bake the gate into the relation so readers structurally cannot bypass it. Create a view (or MV) house_prices_public AS SELECT ... WHERE source_licence <> 'proprietary-tos-restricted' and point every public reader at it; keep the base table for collector/internal paths. New endpoints then inherit the gate for free.

title: One-shot housing takedown command
detail: The kill switches (HOUSING_DROP_LISTINGS_ENABLED, HOUSING_VALUATIONS_ENABLED) exist but a real takedown needs env flip + Upstash cache:housing:* flush + ISR revalidation of /price-drops and suburb pages, spread across Vercel, Cloud Run and the revalidate API. Build a `make housing-takedown` (or an /api/admin/flush-cache target extension — the admin-gated route and TARGETS map already exist at web/src/app/api/admin/flush-cache/route.ts) that executes the flush+revalidate half and prints the exact env-flip commands, so the whole response is one action under time pressure.

title: CI provenance gate blocking committed portal content
detail: The property-crawl work already has a provenance classifier concept ('provenance classifier blocks it' per the crawl memory) but nothing enforces it at commit/CI time — which is exactly how the real New Farm payloads landed in testdata/. Add a cheap CI (and pre-commit) check that fails on staged files matching portal markers: ArgonautExchange, urqlClientCache, listingsMap, UPVSoldListings, realestate.com.au/property-, domain.com.au listing URL shapes — with an allowlist for the synthetic fixtures. Extends naturally to CRAWL_TRACE artifact patterns (traces/**, p*.html).

title: Synthetic portal-fixture builder for extraction tests
detail: The pagemeta extraction tests need the exact REA ArgonautExchange / Domain __NEXT_DATA__ JSON shapes but not real content. Build a small Go fixture generator (testdata builder emitting fake addresses/IDs/prices in the locked payload shapes from crawl_listings_extract.go) shared by both the collector and the services/jobs/internal/jobs/houseprices port, replacing all 4 captured HTML files and removing any future temptation to capture-and-trim live pages into the repo.

title: Licence-gate regression tests over the flag-gated + aggregate surfaces
detail: postgres_suburb_explorer_test.go already proves the pattern (TestHousingLicenceGate_StateSuburbs/_SuburbProfile with testcontainers): extend it with seeded proprietary rows asserting (a) mv_suburb_listing_stats never publishes sub-floor avg/median once the k-floor lands, (b) ListAgencyPriceStats depth suppression below 3 dropped addresses survives MV rebuilds, (c) GetPropertyHistory returns empty under the kill switches, and (d) a grep-style meta-test that every `FROM house_prices` in the store carries the licence predicate (or uses the public view).

title: Admin licence/provenance dashboard panel
detail: The admin jobs page already surfaces sync health; add a small housing-provenance card showing live counts by source_licence across house_prices / property_listings / property_valuations / suburb_crime_stats, the current kill-switch states as the backend actually resolves them (dropListingsEnabled()/valuationsEnabled() readback), and the row-counts of each publishable MV vs its floor. Makes 'what proprietary data do we hold and what of it is publishable right now' a glanceable operator fact instead of a psql session.

title: Housing freshness sentinel workflow over house_price_ingest_runs
detail: The monitoring table already exists and faithfully records per-source status/detail/last_period (it captured both VG failures) — it is simply unwatched. Clone economy-freshness.yml: red on any error-status source in the latest run, on per-source max(period) regression, and on property_price_events silence >3 days. Cheapest possible fix for the class of month-long silent breakage found in this audit.

title: Crawl-derived suburb asking-price medians where VG data is missing or stale
detail: NSW/QLD/WA have zero official suburb medians and VIC is frozen at Dec-2024, yet the crawl corpus now covers 500 suburbs with 88.7k listings and mv_suburb_listing_stats already aggregates per-suburb asking stats. Publishing a clearly-labelled 'median asking price (portal-derived)' series for suburbs lacking VG coverage would fill the biggest data hole on suburb profiles using data already in the DB — as a derived aggregate it stays inside the counts-only/no-republish licence posture already applied to mv_agency_stats.

title: Crime data Phase 2: extend beyond NSW
detail: mv_suburb_crime_latest covers 975 suburbs — 6.4% of the 15,345 in suburb_demographics — because only NSW BOCSAR is ingested (527k rows, FY2025, mode=victim_estimate). The pipeline (000090/000092 + -mode crime, small-pop/unreliable gating) is proven; VIC CSA and QLD QPS publish open LGA/suburb-level tables under compatible licences. Extending to VIC+QLD roughly triples the addressable suburb count for the crime colour-by metric.

title: Route VG fetches (VIC xlsx, NSW PSI zips) through the residential crawl rigs
detail: Both official VG sources are now Cloudflare-blocked from Cloud Run's datacenter IP, while the brandbrain agent rigs on residential Macs already clear Cloudflare/Kasada daily for the listings tier. Adding a 'vg' job kind to the existing counts-only queue (fetch file → parse locally → upsert to house_prices) reuses the whole self-healing agent infrastructure and permanently fixes the fetch-posture problem for any future state VG source.

title: REA sold-disposition detection
detail: 2,497 REA withdrawn listings have unknown disposition (sold vs withdrawn), which is why sold metrics are Domain-only. REA exposes a sold-search SRP per suburb; a low-frequency sold-sweep (monthly, reusing the warmed-Chrome CDP path and smart pagination) could classify recent REA withdrawals and make soldCount/medianSold genuinely cross-portal — the single highest-leverage fix for /price-drops metric fidelity.

title: Per-source data-quality gauges in the crawl run summary
detail: The run-summary log line (crawl_listings.go:386) already counts drops/rises/relists/delists; adding empty-address_key rate, price-parse rate (currently ~34-36% of active listings are unpriced 'contact agent'), and per-portal sold/relist ratios would turn the three portal asymmetries this audit found (sold 0-vs-5,715; relist 1-vs-9,270; addr-key gaps) into visible per-run metrics instead of archaeology.

title: Widen the suburb indexation gate from 1,165 priced suburbs to the full rich-profile corpus
detail: Exists: 15,345 suburb profiles (census rows) with banner heroes (000084, all 15,329 classified), demographics + culture, federal/state electoral representation (000058-60), crime (NSW), amenities/council, politician property cards and OG scene cards — but the sitemap only lists suburbs with latestMedianPrice > 0 (sitemap.ts:545 filter → 1,165 live URLs, all currently 404 per finding 1). These pages are no longer 'thin'. Increment: after fixing the slugs, gate on richer-content signals instead (e.g. population ≥ 200 OR has crime/amenity data), lifting the indexable corpus to ~8-12k pages; add per-state <lastmod>. Value: the single biggest programmatic-SEO lever in the feature (suburb-name + 'house prices'/'demographics'/'crime' queries).

title: Surface the ~12 dark national measures as an 'Affordability & credit' section on /housing
detail: Exists: runOfficial already ingests mortgage_rate_oo/mortgage_rate_investor (RBA F6, rba.go:118), cash_rate (F1.1), housing_credit_growth ×3 (D1), household_dwelling_assets/net_worth/liabilities (E1), wage_index (WPI), rents_index (CPI, abs_affordability.go:26), price_to_income (abs_affordability.go:84), investor_loan_share and price_index_derived — but the web UI charts only mean_price, debt_to_income and median_price (grep measure= across housing pages → 3 distinct). GetHousePriceSeries accepts any measure and HousingSeriesChart already takes a measure prop. Increment: add tiles + WhenVisible charts (mortgage rates vs cash rate, rents inflation YoY, investor vs OO credit growth, price-to-income) and replace the '8-capital price index (to 2021)' tile — frozen upstream — with price_index_derived, which abs.go:368 explicitly built 'to give /housing a current-quarter index line'.

title: Housing embeds + open-data hub listing for the backlink/Dataset-Search program
detail: Exists: a proven embed-backlink program for shorts (/embed/chart, /embed/treemap, /embed/top-shorts, /embed/bank-basket; PR #374 live) and a /data open-data hub with Dataset JSON-LD — but the DATASETS array is shorts-only (grep housing → 0) and no housing embed exists. The ABS/RBA house_prices series are CC-BY (republishable) and the price-drop rollups are own-derived aggregates. Increment: /embed/housing-series (region×measure chart) + /embed/price-drops (state board) with the same attribution-link pattern, plus 2-3 housing Dataset entries (national prices, suburb medians, price-drop aggregates) with CSV endpoints on /data. Value: backlinks from property/finance bloggers + Google Dataset Search visibility for 'australian house prices dataset'.

title: Suburb watchlists + weekly price-cut email digest
detail: Exists: daily property_price_events from the live crawl (~12k listings, 67+ suburbs), mv_suburb_price_drops refreshed per run with instant revalidation (pingRevalidate), a full Resend email stack with broadcasts + HMAC unsubscribe (migrations 000065, PRs #222-#228), user auth, and a stocks-only /alerts page (grep housing → 0). Increment: 'Watch this suburb' on the profile + price-drops rows persisting (user_id, sal_code), and a weekly digest job (new cuts, median move, biggest drop) reusing the broadcast templates. Value: converts one-shot SEO landings into returning users and gives the paid tier a concrete housing perk.

title: Expand the crime layer beyond NSW (VIC/QLD/SA/WA)
detail: Exists: a deliberately state-pluggable pipeline — crime.go builds the SAL registry for ALL states and applies the ABS CVS scaler + ERP denominators, but only crime_nsw.go (BOCSAR) exists as a source; the CrimeCard (suburb-profile.tsx:352-354) and the crime map metrics silently vanish for 10k+ non-NSW suburbs. VIC (Crime Statistics Agency LGA/suburb tables), QLD (QPS open data), SA and WA all publish downloadable offence tables under open licences. Increment: one crime_<state>.go per state feeding the existing compute/rank/gate machinery (000090/000092). Value: the highest-engagement metric on the map toggle, currently available to only ~30% of profiles.

title: Wire the Widow-Maker feature charts to live series and add product CTAs
detail: Exists: the flagship editorial's four visx dashboards run on baked arrays ending 2025 (data/series.ts, dossier dated 2026-06-23) while the live house_prices store now carries every ingredient it charts — cash_rate, mortgage rates, credit growth, price_to_income, debt_to_income — and the HousingSeriesChart format-key pattern already solves the RSC serialization problem. Increment: feed the policy-price and buying-power charts a live-series overlay (baked history + live tail), refresh the stat-strip numbers from GetHousingOverview, and add the missing CTAs into /housing + /price-drops (finding 4). Value: keeps the highest-authority page perpetually current (its meta still says '23 June 2026') and funnels its backlink traffic into the product.

title: Suburb comparison pages ('X vs Y') from the similarity data already computed
detail: Exists: GetSuburbProfile already returns baselines (state/national medians), CompareBar deltas, 'Nearby & comparable' (postcode/price proximity) and 'Similar suburbs' with server-computed similarity scores (data.similar, nationally ranked). Increment: /housing/compare/[a]-vs-[b] pages — two-profile side-by-side (price series overlay via the existing series chart, demographic deltas, crime/electoral contrast) — statically generated for each suburb's top-3 similar/nearby pairs (~5-10k pages, all data from two existing RPCs). Value: 'Bondi vs Bronte' style queries are high-intent, zero-competition programmatic SEO, and the pages interlink the suburb corpus densely.

title: SSR-seed and selectively index the per-address price-history pages
detail: Exists: /housing/property/[addressKey] is live (linked from every address-drops row and suburb Recent-price-drops panel) but deliberately noindex (page.tsx:41) and renders client-side only — the server page ships just a prettified address string. The corpus behind it (~12k property_listings + property_price_events with address_key on ~96% of events, plus the backfill-address mode) is stable and dedup-hardened. Increment: seed the page with an SSR payload (mirror the suburb page's initialProfileJson pattern), then lift noindex for addresses with ≥2 price events and a populated display address. Caveat: this is the one surface where the ToS-restricted crawl licence posture must be re-confirmed before indexing — derived facts only, keep the portal deep-links.

title: Rent tracking: surface rents_index now, add a rental crawl channel later
detail: Exists: the only rent data anywhere is the static Census 2021 median_weekly_rent per suburb and a dark national rents_index (ABS CPI rents, already ingested monthly — abs_affordability.go:26 — never charted). The entire crawl stack (brandbrain queue, -mode agent CDP pollers, suburb catalog, price-event diffing) is channel-agnostic. Increment S: chart rents inflation on /housing and the suburb profile ('Census median vs national rent inflation since 2021'). Increment L: a rental-SRP sweep mode reusing the listings pipeline → suburb advertised median rent + rent-cut events, unlocking a /rents board twin of /price-drops. Value: rental-market queries currently dwarf sale queries and no surface answers them.

title: Reciprocal cross-surface linking mesh (economy ↔ housing ↔ politicians)
detail: Exists: one-way links only — suburb profiles embed SuburbPoliticianPropertyCard (suburb-profile.tsx:184) and /economy hub links /housing once (economy/page.tsx:200), but /economy/[state] has zero housing links, politician profiles never link back to the suburb pages their declared properties sit in (grep '"/housing' in components/politicians → 0), and state suburb explorers never link the state economy page. Increment: a compact housing tile on /economy/[state] (median + YoY from GetHousingOverview via GCCSA_TO_STATE, already fetched on /housing), suburb links on politician property declarations (sal_code is already matched — 335 suburbs live), and an economy link in the state explorer stat strip. Value: distributes the politicians/economy authority into the 15k-page housing corpus and improves crawl depth for finding-1's newly fixed URLs.
